# BTicino C300X Integration v2.9.0b1

## 2026-11-22

[![Support me on Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/img/githubbutton_sm.svg)](https://ko-fi.com/oliver7557)

Beta for firmware 3.0.6, not yet tested on a device. On firmware 1.7.x and
2.0.2 it works like 2.8.2. Includes the bounded RTSP recovery and exact
firewall restoration from 2.8.2. Device/model detection is not part of this beta.

## Display

- **Home Assistant pages on firmware 3.0.6** (beta): the Display patch now
  works on the Qt 5 display of 3.0.6, whose display files are built into the
  vendor program. The home page gets the Alarm and Home Assistant buttons, with
  the Alarm, Home Assistant and Energy pages and the other pages of the
  integration. Switching the optional pages off retains the core display
  hooks; full removal restores the vendor startup script. The touch fix for
  lost taps is not part of it on 3.0.6.
- **Activation and recovery:** apply checks the resources, preload library and
  startup wrapper even when QML is unchanged. Runtime-only agent updates also
  refresh the preload. Failed changes roll back the activation files and their
  quarantine state together, keeping recovery copies if rollback cannot finish.
- **Quarantine:** a qualifying error exit within the first minute starts the stock
  display and disables the overlay. Updates and partial restores do not retry
  it. Installation/settings do not report this fallback as successful
  activation; display follow-up remains pending. Investigate the status and
  log before full removal and an explicit retry. GUI-dependent actions stay
  unavailable during fallback, and missing core activation remains a Repair.
- **Resource integrity:** before registering an overlay, the preload checks
  every resource table, child range, name and payload boundary. Damaged or
  unsupported files are quarantined and the stock resources remain available.

Offline resource-loading and failure-injection checks do not prove device
readiness, vendor C++ signal compatibility or watchdog safety. Cold boot,
fallback/recovery, calls, touch and the Qt 4 regression checks remain device
pre-merge gates. A running GUI process is not proof that every page loaded.
The startup guard is not general reboot-loop protection: crashes after the
first minute (including lazy-loaded pages), hangs and exits 0/137/138/140/143
do not trigger quarantine. SIGKILL/137 can reflect OOM or watchdog termination,
not only an intentional restart. This timing/signal policy is unchanged.
The [offline audit](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-bticino-c300x/blob/v2.9.0b1/docs/audits/firmware-3.0.6-display.md)
records original Qt 5.15.7 resource-loading, all 15 custom components compiling
with substitute vendor types, original signal metadata, and the remaining
device-only checks.
Additional probes exercise the stock and patched wrapper with the original
ARM firmware shell, and alert lifecycle/preemption in original QtQml 5.15.7.
The latter substitutes audio/screen IO and does not establish physical effects.

## Restore Integrity

Routing restoration authenticates the complete original binary and the
current firmware identity, including interrupted patches. Corrupt, truncated
or foreign backups are refused without replacing the target. Restoration
uses a private staging directory and verifies the installed stock result.
The Qt5 forwarding label is restored through its RCC overlay, not skipped.
Failed label restoration blocks routing restoration; inactive labels are not
advertised as applied. Removing a label retains any unrelated quarantine.
Agent removal now verifies or restores stock routing before deleting recovery
files. If that fails, the agent files and backups remain for recovery; a
verified stock target needs no backup or unnecessary rewrite.
Complete display removal also works with a missing or damaged extraction
cache: it restores the original wrapper and removes the overlay directly,
without requiring the resource packer. Partial removal still preserves the
remaining overlay and its quarantine.
Qt5 wrapper installation and recovery require the complete known original
firmware wrapper hash. Empty, modified, truncated or already-patched backups
are refused; the copied recovery candidate and installed original are checked
again before success. The original must also be executable; invalid originals
are refused before activation writes begin. Unknown custom wrappers are not
silently accepted.

## Install

1. Back up Home Assistant.
2. Enable **Pre-release** for this repository in Marketplace, or beta versions
   in HACS (**Redownload**), and install 2.9.0b1.
3. Run the agent update Repair, then switch on **Home Assistant pages on the
   display** under **Configure > Display > Display and Display patch**. The
   display restarts once.

To go back on firmware 3.0.6, first remove the **complete** overlay with the
beta's `qml_patch.sh restore-all`, and confirm that `qt5_overlay` is `off` and
the stock display is running. Switching off the optional pages alone is not
enough. Only then install the stable release and run its agent update Repair:
stable 2.8.2 does not contain the Qt 5 overlay or its recovery code.
The updated beta native updater now rejects targets without Qt 5 recovery
(`qt5_recovery_required`) until the overlay, preload and quarantine are gone
and the complete executable vendor start script is verified. Rejection leaves
the installed agent and recovery files untouched. Updates to a Qt 5-capable
beta remain possible and retain quarantine. This guard is not retroactive:
older agents and direct SSH/manual installs still require careful full removal
first. Do not downgrade with an active, incomplete or quarantined overlay.

## Feedback

Please report how the display behaves: whether the buttons and pages appear,
whether taps and pages work, and whether calls and messages still work as
before. Attach the Display patch status, the integration diagnostics and, if
you can reach the device, `/tmp/c300x-display-qt5.log`. Details:
[Display patch on firmware 3.0.6](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-bticino-c300x/blob/v2.9.0b1/docs/advanced-maintenance.md#display-patch-on-firmware-306).
